origins.section: A Scenario Is a Copy With Its Own Snapshot, Never an Edit of Another Scenario
Post-Opt Reads the Plan, and Every Override Sends the Scenario Back for a Rerun
Budget Lock Freezes the Plan of Record, and a Change Means a New Scenario

gates.says: all 3 of this quiz's answerable readings held and each was taken over the question as it stands

recorded.prompt:q-copy-id: Read the whole lesson page, then this question. Using only what the page states, which option does the page decide is correct? Quote or cite the deciding passage.
recorded.outcome:q-copy-id: 'The copy starts with the base's snapshot, because its inputs are identical'. 'any change to... a solver setting gives a different one.'
recorded.prompt:q-late-change: Read the whole lesson page, then this question. Using only what the page states, which option does the page decide is correct? Quote or cite the deciding passage.
recorded.outcome:q-late-change: An override 'goes into the scenario, gives a new snapshot, sends the scenario back to Pre-Opt, and needs a rerun'.
recorded.prompt:q-after-lock: Read the whole lesson page, then this question. Using only what the page states, which option does the page decide is correct? Quote or cite the deciding passage.
recorded.outcome:q-after-lock: 'A locked scenario refuses edits; a change after lock needs a copy, which goes through the cycle again.'

A cue decides only when it clearly singles out one option over every other; a weak cue, or one another option shares, decides nothing. Otherwise answer 'none'. Say which cue decided it, or that none did.
